742:
The following words, terms, and phrases when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning.
Approved heavy wrecker service means an approved wrecker service whose equipment list includes a wrecker rated to tow a heavy vehicle.
Approved wrecker service means any wrecker service that submits a successful application under this article, and which otherwise complies with the provisions hereof to qualify for the privilege of engagement by the Habersham County Sheriffs Office (hereinafter sometimes referred to as "HCSO") for the removal or storage of vehicles.
County means Habersham County, Georgia.
Damaged vehicles means any motor vehicle suffering such mechanical or structural damage to the extent that it cannot properly or safely be operated.
Heavy motor vehicle means any motor vehicle weighing over 10,000 of gross vehicle weight.
Passenger vehicle means any motor vehicle weighing up to 10,000 of gross vehicle weight.
Sheriff's office or HCSO means the Habersham County Sheriffs Office, its officers, agents, or employees.
Property owner means the owner of the property, or his authorized representative, upon which a vehicle to be removed is located.
Response time means the time the wrecker service arrives at the scene of the incident after a call is received from the requesting agency to respond. This time should not exceed 30 minutes.
Undamaged vehicle means any vehicle that has no or only minor structural or mechanical damage and is capable of being safely and properly operated.
Vehicle owner means the owner of a vehicle or his authorized representative.
Wrecker means an automotive vehicle with hoisting apparatus and equipment used for the purpose of towing damaged, wrecked, disabled, or abandoned motor vehicles.
Wrecker service means any entity, corporation, partnership, or individual person, whether as principal, agent or employee in the business of removing, towing and/or storing motor vehicles abandoned in the roadway or on other public lands, or wrecked or disabled motor vehicles by the use of a wrecker and properly licensed by the state.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
743:
Removal of motor vehicles from privately owned real property shall be regulated by the Georgia Department of Motor Vehicle Safety, as provided in O.C.G.A. §44-1-13.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
744:
Each wrecker service desiring to be added to the county-approved wrecker service list or the approved heavy wrecker service list to respond to calls for wrecker services from the county shall make application to the sheriff's office annually for approved wrecker permit. The sheriff or his designee shall accept applications for approved wrecker permits annually from September 1 through October 31 for permits to be valid for the subsequent calendar year. The application shall be submitted on a form provided by the sheriffs office. No application shall be processed unless all required documents have been submitted. Such application shall include, but not be limited to, the following information:
(1) Listing of name and address of the owner of the wrecker service. If held by a corporation or limited liability company, the names and addresses of its officers or managers and any stockholders or members holding 20 percent or more of the corporate stock or membership interest. If held by a partnership, a listing of the names and addresses of all partners.
(2) Certificate of six months of pre-paid insurance coverage showing compliance with the requirements in this article.
(3) A copy of the fee schedule to be in effect for the calendar year of the permit to be sought.
(4) A copy of the current valid occupational tax certificate or business license from the county and a permit from the Georgia Department of Motor Vehicle Safety, as well as proof of insurance on the companies vehicles.
(5) Complete list of addresses of all impound/vehicle storage sites to be utilized by the wrecker service.
(6) Drivers history and background checks on any and all drivers for the wrecker service.
(7) A minimum of two wreckers to be considered for approval.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
745:
(a) [Examination of application.] Upon receipt of a timely and complete application for an approved wrecker service permit or an approved heavy wrecker service permit, the sheriff's office shall examine the application for completeness, request any omitted required information, perform any necessary investigation, and inspect the equipment, storage lot(s) and business location for the applicant. Thereafter, the sheriff shall approve or deny the application.
(b) Denial. The sheriff shall have the due cause to deny any application for an approved wrecker service permit or approved heavy wrecker service permit for the following reasons:
(1) The application has remained incomplete for 30 days due to the failure of the applicant to provide any paper or document required in the application or requested additional information.
(2) The applicant has provided false information in the application.
(3) The applicant, during the preceding 12 months from the application date, had a wrecker service business license held by such owner revoked for cause by the state or by any political subdivision thereof, or the business or owner of the business has been convicted by any court of competent jurisdiction of engaging in unfair business practices with respect to the operation of any wrecker service.
(4) The applicant does not have an impound facility as required in this article.
(5) The applicant, if the applicant is an individual, has a conviction of any violent felony, or any serious driving offense as defined in O.C.G.A. §40-6-15, or currently has a suspended or revoked driver's license.
If the sheriff denies any application for an approved wrecker permit or approved heavy wrecker permit, he shall do so in writing and shall notify the applicant of his decision and reasons for his decision.
(c) Approval. If the sheriff does not deny any timely and complete application for one or more reasons stated in paragraph (a) of this section, then he shall approve the application and issue the requested approved wrecker permit or approved heavy wrecker permit to the applicant. Any application not denied within 60 days after a complete application has been filed with the sheriff's office, shall be deemed approved.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
746:
At the conclusion of the annual application and permitting process, the sheriff's office shall compile an annual list of approved wrecker services and approved heavy wrecker services. Every approved heavy wrecker service shall be shown on both lists. The sheriff's office shall make use of the wrecker services on a rotating on-call basis for incidents where the owner of any vehicle does not have a preference for a wrecker service to be utilized. Each permit holder on the approved wrecker service list shall be utilized on a rotational basis per incident on an equal rotating basis. Each permit holder on the approved heavy wrecker service list shall be utilized on a rotational basis per incident in an equal rotating basis, for towing of heavy motor vehicles whenever the on-call approved wrecker service is not also an approved heavy wrecker service.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
747:
It shall be unlawful for any wrecker service, whether an approved wrecker service, or not, to respond to sheriff's office calls for wrecker assistance on the streets of the county without complying with the provisions of this article. In unusual or emergency situations if the on-call wrecker service determines that it is in need of additional assistance from another wrecker service, the on-call wrecker service may seek assistance from any wrecker service that has been approved by the sheriff's office under the provisions of this article.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
748:
All wreckers that operate upon any of the streets of the county shall be clearly identified as such, with the name and domicile of the wrecker service operating the wrecker.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
749:
No wrecker shall go to any incident scene unless:
(1) Called by the sheriff's office.
(2) Called by the vehicle owner.
(3) There exists an extreme emergency immediately endangering life or property; or
(4) Called by the property owner where vehicle is located.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
750:
No wrecker service shall proceed to an incident scene by reason of any information received by monitoring sheriff's office calls.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
751:
(a) Wrecker services shall determine the method and manner of removing vehicles; provided, however, that they shall exercise due care in removal operations and shall follow the direction of the sheriff's deputy directing the removal so as not to impede or endanger the general public and property.
(b) The driver of each wrecker towing away any motor vehicle from the scene or a wreck shall also take away all parts belonging to the motor vehicle which is being towed away, or, if they consist of small parts or broken glass, the driver shall clear the streets of said small parts and glass, unless the driver is ordered not to do so by the investigating deputy due to circumstances at the scene of the accident. No additional fee may be charged for this clean up.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
752:
(a) Whenever any wrecked or abandoned motor vehicle is removed without the request, direction or participation of the sheriff's office, the wrecker service performing the removal shall, if the owner is unknown, within the 72 hours of such removal, furnish to the sheriff's office the following information with respect to such motor vehicle: Tag number and description, including year, make, model, color and vehicle identification number.
(b) The wrecker service shall notify the motor vehicle owner of the time and place of removal and of the present whereabouts of the vehicle, as required by O.C.G.A § 04-11-1 et seq.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
753:
Whenever any motor vehicle is removed by a wrecker service at the direction of a deputy sheriff, the deputy sheriff shall make a thorough inventory of all equipment, accessories, personal articles and other items either attached to or located within the motor vehicle. Such inventory shall be completed on a form supplied by the sheriff's office and signed by the deputy in charge of the removal. Upon acceptance of the motor vehicle and prior to its removal, the agent or employee of the wrecker service performing the removal shall sign the inventory form. The deputy shall retain the original and the wrecker service shall retain a copy.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
754:
When specifically directed to do so by a deputy sheriff, the wrecker service shall hold the motor vehicles for evidence, confiscation or any other purposes permitted by law. Upon the written and signed authorization of the sheriff's office on a form prescribed by the sheriff's office, the wrecker service shall release any motor vehicle so held to the owner, his authorized representative, or other person entitled by law to possession of the vehicle.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
755:
(a) A motor vehicle owner in ordinary, non-emergency situations may engage a private wrecker service of their choice to remove their motor vehicle. The responding deputy shall advise the motor vehicle owner of his option to call the wrecker service of their choice that is capable of responding in a reasonable amount of time.
(b) If the owner states no preference, the deputy sheriff shall request the 911 dispatching center to call the approved wrecker service that is on duty in the rotation.
(c) If the owner states no preference, and if a heavy motor vehicle must be towed, the deputy sheriff shall request the 911 dispatching center to call the approved heavy duty wrecker service on duty in the rotation.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
756:
(a) Each impound facility of the applying or approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service must be located within Habersham County and shall be owned or leased by the applicant.
(b) The gate to the impound lot shall be locked and remain locked during the hours of darkness except to provide ingress and egress in connection with wrecker service operations.
(c) Each approved wrecker service and each approved heavy wrecker service shall submit to the sheriff's office an inventory of all vehicles remaining in its possession whose owner has not been identified or notified. The inventory shall be submitted within seven days if any request by the sheriff's office but not less frequently than every six months and shall be completed on a form supplied or approved by the county.
(d) The requirements for the impound facility of any approved wrecker service permit holder and any approved heavy wrecker service permit holder are as follows:
(1) Impoundment must be located at a property zoned location within Habersham County and in compliance with the applicable zoning and land use laws, rules, regulations and ordinances.
(2) The impound facility shall operate under a valid Habersham county business license.
(3) The entire impound lot must be adequately illuminated during the hours of darkness to discourage and detect attempts at that or vandalism.
(4) The impound facility shall be fully enclosed with all fencing (and gates) being at least six feet tall and made of chain link or wood, with gates that can be securely locked. An attendant for every approved wrecker service impound facility shall be available to provide service at the impound lot Monday through Friday each week 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
(5) A wrecker service impound facility is not required to keep business hours on Saturday or Sunday or on legal holidays.
(6) Wrecker services are required to provide two separate contacts and numbers for individuals wishing to retrieve their vehicle outside of business hours.
(e) Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to prohibit the sheriff's office from providing its own impoundment facility upon county property for the purpose of storing or holding vehicles for evidence, confiscation, or any other purpose permitted by law.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
757:
Approved wrecker services and approved heavy wrecker services shall carry liability insurance policies in compliance with the requirements of the Georgia Department of Motor Vehicle Safety for loss or damage occasioned by negligence or misfeasance on the part of the wrecker service and name Habersham County and the Habersham County Sheriff's Office as additional insureds. Such policies shall be provided to the sheriff's office and the county upon request and should be within the minimum scope as follows:
(a) Intrastate:
(1) $100,000.00/Person.
(2) $300,000.00/Accident.
(3) $50,000.00/Property.
(4) $50,000.00/Garage Keepers Liability Insurance (GKLL) (Liability insurance which covers stored vehicles and contents, must be maintained on each impound or storage lot(s) sufficient to cover the actual value of all stored vehicles towed or removed to such lot or storage facility).
Such policies shall also provide full loss, theft, or damage with respect to any motor vehicle or to equipment, accessories, personal articles, or other items whether attached to or located within a motor vehicle removed and/or stored while such motor vehicle is in the custody, control and possession of the wrecker service.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
758:
(a) Should a mistake be made in good faith by the sheriff's office or the 911 dispatching center in dispatching the wrong wrecker service, no charge can be made by the wrong wrecker service for such response or the return to place of business unless such wrecker service actually performs the removal of the motor vehicle.
(b) Where the investigating deputy of the sheriff's office at any incident scene determines that the on-call wrecker service has failed to appear at the scene within 30 minutes of the request for service, the deputy shall have the option to cancel the request for service to the rotation wrecker service, and to place a request for service with the approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service next in the rotation.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
759:
The provisions of this section apply to all work performed for any customer of an approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service when service is requested by the sheriff's office. No fees other than those authorized by this section may be charged for towing when called upon to do so by the sheriff's office.
(a) No approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service shall charge in excess of $40.00 per day for storage of a passenger vehicle or heavy motor vehicle.
(b) No approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service shall charge for the first 24 hours that the vehicle was stored in any lot.
(c) No approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service shall charge for any day the wrecker service impound lot is closed and the owner of the vehicle is unable to claim his vehicle.
(d) An approved wrecker service may charge an after-hours fee of $50.00 outside of normal business hours, when a vehicle owner wants to claim their vehicle.
(e) No approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service shall store vehicles at a location other than the secure impound lot submitted with the application for sheriff's office approval without written prior approval of the sheriff's office.
(f) No approved wrecker service or approved heavy wrecker service shall charge in excess of the following amounts for a tow:

(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
760:
(a) Each wrecker service approved under the provisions of this article shall have the following minimum equipment in operating condition:
(1) A roll back wrecker rated at one ton or greater or a wrecker rated at one ton or greater with a wheel lift and a winch rated at four tons or greater.
(2) Each approved heavy wrecker service shall additionally have a wrecker rated for the towing of heavy motor vehicles.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
761:
With 24 hours' notice, the sheriff or his designee may temporarily suspend the permit right of any wrecker service permit holder to respond to calls from the county for violations of this article, or for any conduct by the wrecker service permit holder that threatens the public safety, property or interferes with the efficient operation of the sheriff's office. The permit holder shall be entitled to a hearing before the sheriff upon written request for a hearing by the permit holder. The permit holder shall request such a hearing within ten calendar days of notification of the suspension by the sheriff or his designee; otherwise, the suspension shall be deemed a revocation of the permit. The permit holder shall be provided with five days advanced written notice of the hearing date by hand delivery or certified mail return receipt requested. The hearing before the sheriff shall be held within 14 days of such written request by the permit holder. At the hearing the sheriff may reinstate the permit, continue the suspension, or revoke the permit.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
762:
Violations of the provisions of this article shall be heard in the Magistrate Court of Habersham County and subject to the penalties set forth in the Code of Habersham County, Georgia. Each day such violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense.
(Ord. of 12-18-2023, § 1)
1003:
All persons or firms harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of Habersham County for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside this state shall provide notice of such harvesting operations (hereinafter referred to as "Notice") to the board of commissioners of Habersham County or its designee—the county manager of Habersham County ("hereinafter referred to as "the county") by giving said notice to the county manager for Habersham County prior to entering onto the property, if possible, but in no event later than 24 hours after entering onto the property. Further, such persons shall give notice of cessation of cutting within 24 hours after the job is completed.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1005:
Subject to the provisions of section 70-105 hereof, notice may be submitted in person, by transmission of an electronic record via telefacsimile or e-mail or by mail.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1006:
Subject to the provisions of section 70-105 hereof, upon notification published by the director of the Georgia Forestry Commission that a state-wide notification website or platform is available for public use, persons or firms wishing to utilize said website or platform to provide notice may do so at their option and Habersham County will accept notifications submitted in this manner.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1007:
On and after a date specified and published by the director of the Georgia Forestry Commission, use of the state-wide notification website or platform shall be mandatory and shall be the sole means of providing the notice; on and after said date, submission of the notice by any of the means listed in section 70-103 above shall cease and will no longer be deemed acceptable or in compliance with this Code section.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1008:
The notice shall not be or remain effective unless and until the person or firm providing such notice has delivered to the county a valid surety bond, executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in this state, protecting Habersham County against any damage caused by such person or firm in the amount of $5,000.00; provided, however, that at the option of the person or firm harvesting timber, a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association as defined in O.C.G.A. §7-1-4 in the amount of $5,000.00 may be provided in lieu of a surety bond. Such bonds or letters of credit shall be subject to the conditions set forth in sections 70-107 and 70-108 of this section. No more than one bond or letter of credit shall be required from each person or firm harvesting timber, regardless of the number of tracts harvested in the county for so long as the bond or letter of credit remains in effect. The bond or letter of credit required herein shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it was delivered.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1009:
The bond or letter of credit required by section 70-106 of this section shall protect Habersham County against any damage requiring re-ditching or repair of existing ditch structures or the removal of any harvesting residue, including treetops, debris, logs, pulpwood and other materials, placed in or around the county's rights-of-way caused by such person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall be available to reimburse the county for any cost incurred to repair such damage or remove such debris in or around the county's rights-of-way. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall also be available to reimburse the county for any costs incurred to maintain or repair county roads damaged by the ingress or egress of motor vehicles engaged in the harvest operations located within 500 feet of any point of ingress or egress of the timber harvesting operation. The right of Habersham County to call such bond or letter of credit in accordance with the provisions of sectin 70-108 of this section shall be in addition to any other remedies available to the county at law or in equity for damage to county roads or rights-of-way.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1010:
When damage results from a person or firm's harvesting activities, the county shall make and provide a written claim to the person or firm causing the damage within 30 business days after the county becomes aware of the damage. Such claim may be given in person, by telefacsimile, email or mail. The claim shall describe the damage in detail and, in compliance with section 70-109(a) of this section, give the person or firm the opportunity to repair such damage within 30 days of the notification; provided, however, the county shall be authorized to repair the damage immediately if the county determines the conditions present a threat to public safety, health or welfare and, upon making such repairs, shall present to the person or firm and the issuer of the applicable bond or letter of credit an itemized list of expenses incurred as a claim against the responsible party and the issuer of its bond or letter of credit. Upon the issuance of a claim as provided in this section the county shall notify the issuer of the bond or letter of credit that a claim has been made and will be resolved or adjudicated according to the terms of this section.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1011:
Within 30 days of receipt of the written claim described in section 70-108, the person or firm against whom the claim is submitted may:
(a) Repair such damage at his or its own expense with the approval and supervision of the county. When repairs are completed to the satisfaction of the county, the county shall provide a written notification of satisfactory completion within five business days to the responsible person or firm and to the surety issuing the bond or the bank issuing the letter of credit, thereby terminating the claim.
(b) In the event of inclement weather or other factors preventing repair of the damage, request a 30 day extension to repair the damage from the county, provided that no extensions shall exceed 90 days from the date the claim was tendered. Approval of any extension shall be at the discretion of the county.
(c) Appeal the claim to the Magistrate Court of Habersham County. Any such appeal must name the issuer of the bond or letter of credit as a party, who shall be served with all pleadings in the action and shall have the right to appear. The court will hear evidence and arguments within 30 days of the written appeal and issue a ruling within ten days of such hearing. Any such appeal shall toll the 30 day period, or any extension thereof, required by section 70-108 of this section. If the court rules in favor of the person or firm against whom the claim was made, the county shall have no right to recover any proceeds of the bond or letter of credit and judgment shall be entered against the county. If the court rules in favor of the county, the court shall determine the amount of damages to which the county is entitled to recover and enter judgment accordingly; the county shall be authorized to call the bond or letter of credit and recover from the proceeds thereof an amount equal to the judgment entered by the court up to the total amount of the bond or letter of credit. The portion of any judgment entered in favor of the county that exceeds the amount of the bond or letter of credit shall be subject to collection by any additional remedies at law or equity.
(d) In the event the person or firm against whom the claim has been submitted fails to take any of the actions allowed under subparagraphs (a), (b) or (c) of this paragraph within the time required therein, such person or firm shall be deemed to have waived any and all rights to contest the call of the bond or letter of credit.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1012:
If the person or firm tendering a bond or letter of credit pursuant to the requirements of this section continues its timber harvesting operation beyond the calendar year in which the bond or letter of credit was issued, the person or firm continuing the timber harvesting operation shall tender a new bond or letter of credit within five business days after the first day of the new calendar year.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1013:
In the event a bond or letter of credit tendered pursuant to the requirements of this section is revoked by the surety or bank, then a valid replacement bond or letter of credit must be delivered to the county within five business days after the date of revocation in order for timber harvesting operations to continue. In addition, if the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit caused its revocation, the amount of the bond or letter of credit required shall be increased to $7,500.00 after the first revocation and $10,000.00 after a second revocation caused by the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The maximum amount of the bond or letter of credit shall not exceed $10,000.00.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1014:
Submission of the notice shall authorize the person or firm submitting same to undertake the timber harvesting operation described in the notice and shall remain in effect until such time as the person or firm gives notice that the harvesting operation is complete; provided, however, that any change in the facts required to be provided for purposes of such notice, including, but not limited to, a change in the scope or extent of the operation, must be reported to the county within three business days after such change.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1015:
Any person or firm that engages in a timber harvesting operation in the unincorporated portion of Habersham County without complying with the notice requirements of this section shall be subject to a citation and trial and, upon conviction, shall be fined in an amount not to exceed $1,500.00 for each violation.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1016:
This section applies to activities which qualify as forestry land management practices or agricultural operations under O.C.G.A. §12-7-17(5) and (6) on land that is zoned for or used for forestry, silvicultural or agricultural purposes. It shall not authorize land disturbing activities incidental to development in conflict with the limitations set forth in O.C.G.A. §12-7-17(6),
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
1017:
Consistent with O.C.G.A. §12-6-24:
(a) No fee shall be charged to provide and submit the notice; and
(b) No permit, including a driveway permit, shall be required of the person or firm engaged in a timber harvesting operation as defined by said Georgia code section. Persons and firms providing the notice may be asked to consult with county officials responsible for roads and public works for the purpose of minimizing damage to the county's roads, rights-of-way and infrastructure and are urged to follow recommendations from county officials. Notwithstanding the forgoing, the person or firm conducting the timber harvest operation bears ultimate responsibility for their actions and nothing in this section shall preclude the county from taking any and all legal action necessary to protect its property and the health, safety and welfare of its citizens.
(Ord. of 6-19-2023, § 1)
